newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton ends lower on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton ends lower on poor demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices dropped on Friday on poor demand, dealers said.
"Sluggish mill buying dragged prices down," one trader said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell 10 rupees at 870/920 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned dropped by 10/35 rupees to 1,525/1,650 rupees per maund.
F-414 slid by 5 rupees to 1,920/1,935 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan rose to 13,000/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 12,600/13,000 rupees.
"Gujarat cotton bounced back from lower levels on shortage of ready stock due to a drop in arrivals," one trader said.
The Bombay cotton market is closed on Monday for a Hindu festival (festival of colour).
